I'm sure many of us have gone through some sort of a Harry Potter fanfiction phase (it's not just me, right? ...Right?).

So! Methods of Rationality aside, what are some of your favorite works? It's a bit of a cliche, but Make a Wish never fails to make me laugh.

I love fanfiction! If it's a phase, it's one I've never recovered from. I tend to stay in some weirder, smaller parts of the fanfic world, particularly for the Oliver Wood/Katie Bell ship. My favorites are Neurotically Obsessed (sadly abandoned) and A Whiff of Competition (unfinished but last updated fairly recently).

At this point, HPMoR seems like such an endeavor I'm not sure if it's worth reading.

Believe me, it's not worth reading. If you like reading about how harry is a genius and everybody else is a brain dead zombie, and how things that usually take months or years to plan somehow manage to be planned and executed within a couple hours, and how an eleven year old is somehow emotionally and mentally experienced and mature enough to make Dumbledore look like a wailing toddler, this book is for you.

The author uses HPMOR as his soapbox, too, so there will be long pages of nothing but Harry explaining things that people just NEED to know but aren't even remotely connected to the plot, while Hermione plays the idiot lackey who asks "Who? What? Why?" when the author wants his theoretical audience to ask him more about his hypothetical scenario.

To be fair, the grammar is fine and the plot moves along steadily, which is more than I can say about most fanfiction.

To go the Goldilocks route, HPMoR isn't a perfect, end-all fanfiction that some make it out to be, but it's definitely worth a look, in my opinion. Especially the first few chapters. Get to the bit where Harry reacts to Time Turners and you'll see what I mean.

And thanks for the recommendation! Weird pairings are great - it's almost closer to the fiction part than the fan part :)

Here's a decently tough one: how do you find out if a linked list has a cycle, using constant extra memory and linear time?

depending on the implementation, just check the last element if it has a link to the first element. If it's a single link list, then you just iterate until you get to the first element again.

So for a doubly linked list the time complexity for checking should be O(1), for singly linked lists(depending on implemtation again) it should be O(n).
